channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan's dollar exchange rate increases again
item.description: The dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has risen again. The Central Bank of Uzbekistan announced the exchange rates of foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective September 25.

item.title: US sanctions force Iranian plane to return to Tehran
item.description: An Iranian plane was forced to return to Tehran due to US sanctions. The specific details of the incident and the nature of the sanctions were not provided in the source.

item.title: Yandex Go Partners with 700 Drivers with Hearing and Speech Impairments in Uzbekistan
item.description: Yandex Go is collaborating with 700 drivers who have hearing and speech impairments in Uzbekistan, completing 850,000 trips over five years. The service is adapted for these drivers, featuring phone-call-free connections, sign language training, and text-based communication. This initiative aims to enhance accessibility and employment opportunities.

item.title: 47 Chinese-Made Buses Arrive in Urgench, Uzbekistan for Public Transport
item.description: Forty-seven modern buses, including 32 Zhongtong and 15 Yutong models, have been imported to Uzbekistan's Khorezm region. These buses were purchased by local transport companies and are intended for use on internal routes within the city of Urgench. This acquisition is part of a broader effort to renew bus fleets across the country.

item.title: Former Bishkek Vice-Mayor Azamat Kadyrov Accused of Abuse of Office
item.description: Former Bishkek Vice-Mayor Azamat Kadyrov is accused of abuse of his official position. This information emerged from a court ruling regarding the selection of a pre-trial detention measure for the suspect. The specific details of the alleged abuse have not been fully disclosed.

item.title: Uzbek Banker Kahramonjon Olimov Placed on International Wanted List
item.description: Uzbek financier and Anorbank shareholder Kahramonjon Olimov has been placed on an international wanted list, with his Red Notice published on the Interpol website. The notice does not specify the charges or the requesting country. The Insider previously reported Olimov was arrested in absentia in Uzbekistan for kidnapping.

item.title: Number of Tajik-Invested Companies in Uzbekistan Exceeds 100
item.description: The number of companies with Tajik investment in Uzbekistan has increased by over 100. Currently, 483 enterprises with Tajik capital operate in Uzbekistan, while 116 companies with Uzbek capital are active in Tajikistan.

item.title: New 'Keskanyor' Border Post to Open Between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A new 'Keskanyor' border post will be established on the border between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has tasked officials to develop the project and commence construction within three months.

item.title: Tajikistan and Russia Agree on Mutual Recognition of Customs Control Results
item.description: Tajikistan's Customs Service and Russia's Federal Customs Service signed a protocol for mutual electronic recognition of customs control results. The agreement aims to enhance customs cooperation, expand digital technologies, and simplify procedures.

item.title: New executives introduced at Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Construction
item.description: Nurdan Oruntaev, the Minister of Construction, Architecture, Housing, and Communal Services of Kyrgyzstan, has introduced new executives to the ministry's staff. The personnel changes were announced by the minister.

item.title: Uzbek Investors Visit Dangara Free Economic Zone in Tajikistan
item.description: A delegation of investors from Uzbekistan visited the Dangara Free Economic Zone (FEZ) in Tajikistan to explore investment opportunities and production potential. Discussions focused on expanding economic cooperation, attracting direct investment, and establishing joint projects. Both sides emphasized shared historical and cultural ties.

item.title: Uzbekistan Eliminates Business Plan Requirement for Loans Up to 500 Million Som
item.description: Uzbekistan will no longer require business plans for loans up to 500 million soums, shifting focus to real cash flow assessment. State banks will now evaluate creditworthiness based on order books, turnover, and business chain connections, rather than solely on traditional collateral.

item.title: One killed in Badakhshan after Russian tourist convoy vehicle hits motorcycle
item.description: A motorcycle rider was killed in Badakhshan province when a vehicle from a Russian tourist convoy collided with the motorcycle. The Taliban have detained four foreign tourists and two interpreters in connection with the incident.

item.title: Uzbekistan tax authorities to assist businesses with declining revenue or jobs
item.description: Uzbekistan's tax authorities will now assist businesses experiencing reduced revenue or job losses. Local tax inspectors will investigate causes and propose solutions with regional officials. Measures include tax deferrals, loan extensions, and export assistance.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Open New Border Post 'Keskanyor' with Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to open the 'Keskanyor' border post, twice the size of 'Dostlik', with Kyrgyzstan. An agreement has been reached, with project development and construction to begin within three months. This aims to triple cargo volume and halve transit times. Additionally, construction of a paid Tashkent-Andijan highway is slated to start in 2027.

item.title: Tajikistan and China to Expand Cooperation in Science and Technology
item.description: Tajikistan and China held a working meeting to discuss scientific and technological cooperation, including joint initiatives within the 'One Belt, One Road' and SCO frameworks. Key areas include water resources, ecology, climate change, and digital technologies. Both sides explored possibilities for joint research projects and academic exchanges.

item.title: New 'Keskaner' Border Crossing Point to Appear Between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A new border crossing point, 'Keskaner,' will be established between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, doubling the size of the current 'Dostlik' crossing. This is expected to triple cargo traffic and reduce border crossing times significantly. The project is linked to increased transport flows, including the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway.

item.title: China and Russia Account for Over Half of Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Trade Turnover
item.description: In January-July 2026, Kyrgyzstan's foreign trade turnover exceeded $10 billion. China and Russia remain the primary economic partners, accounting for over 60% of the total trade volume. Exports grew significantly in July, driven by precious metals, ores, textiles, and agricultural goods, with Russia being the largest buyer.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan recognized for best tax environment for innovators in Asia-Pacific
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's High Technology Park has received the Startup Ecosystem Awards 2026 in the Asia-Pacific category for "Best Tax Environment for Innovators." The award highlights the country's supportive policies for technological advancement.

item.title: 19 Kazakh servicemen swept away at Caspian Sea training exercise
item.description: Nineteen Kazakh servicemen were swept away during a training exercise near the Caspian Sea coast. Nine individuals have died, and three have been rescued. The incident occurred during drills on the Caspian Sea shore.

item.title: Money changer killed by unidentified gunmen in Afghanistan's Ghazni province
item.description: Local sources reported that a money changer, identified as Gulbuddin, was shot dead by unknown gunmen in the Wali Dad village of Qarabagh district, Ghazni province. The man was inside his vehicle when the attack occurred. His father reportedly works for the Taliban police headquarters in Ghazni.

item.title: Kazakhstani Sailors Lost at Sea During Caspian Exercises; Nine Dead
item.description: During naval exercises in the Caspian Sea on September 24, a wave swept away Kazakhstani servicemen in the Mangistau region. Nine military personnel died in the incident, according to reports.

item.title: Tajikistan Presents Labor Migration Approaches at Budapest Process Conference
item.description: A representative from Tajikistan's Migration Service attended the Budapest Process conference in Islamabad, focusing on legal migration pathways, migrant rights, and migration management. The meeting discussed enhancing cooperation between government bodies, employers, and international organizations to create safe and organized labor migration mechanisms.

item.title: Former Afghan President Karzai Condemns Pakistani Airstrikes as Aggression
item.description: Former Afghan President Hamid Karzai denounced Pakistani airstrikes on Kandahar, Khost, and Paktia provinces as "aggression." He urged Islamabad to abandon this policy and pursue good neighborly relations, warning of consequences. The Taliban also condemned the attacks, vowing retaliation.

item.title: Tajikistan Defense Minister Demands Quality Autumn Conscription
item.description: Tajikistan's Defense Minister, Colonel General Emomali Sobirzoda, has called for a high-quality autumn conscription drive. The directive was issued during a methodological training meeting focused on preparing for the conscription of citizens into the armed forces. Favorable service conditions were also highlighted.

item.title: UN General Assembly Discusses Artificial Intelligence Risks and Control
item.description: Artificial intelligence was a key topic at the UN General Assembly's 81st session, with world leaders warning about autonomous weapons, disinformation, and job losses. Disagreements emerged on control, with the US favoring competition and others calling for international rules and state oversight.

item.title: Andijan to Establish Special Fund for Women's Employment with $20 Million
item.description: A special fund will be established in Andijan to ensure women's employment, with $20 million allocated. This initiative aims to create separate financial and organizational opportunities for women's employment in the region.

item.title: Regional Competition for Female Civil Servants Held in Dangara District
item.description: A regional tour of the Republican Competition 'Best Female Civil Servant' took place in Dangara district on September 22, 2026. Participants were assessed on political knowledge, legal education, professional skills, and communication etiquette, reflecting state policy to enhance women's role in public service.

item.title: Andijan to Invest 100 Billion Soums in Fruit and Vegetable Processing
item.description: Andijan plans to allocate 100 billion soums for fruit and vegetable processing, aiming to reach a 30% processing level by providing small processing equipment to the public on lease, as decided in a presidential meeting.

item.title: Taliban spokesman: Pakistani airstrikes killed four civilians in Afghanistan
item.description: Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid stated that four civilians were killed in Pakistani airstrikes on Kandahar, Paktia, and Khost provinces. He condemned the attacks as a "blatant act of aggression" and vowed they would not go unanswered. Pakistan's information minister claimed the strikes were in response to drones entering Pakistani territory.

item.title: Central Asia Internet Connectivity Forum CAPIF 5 kicks off in Dushanbe
item.description: The fifth Central Asia Connectivity and Peering Forum (CAPIF 5) began in Dushanbe on September 24, 2026. This is the first time the event is held in Tajikistan. The forum brings together internet community representatives, providers, operators, IXPs, government bodies, and IT specialists from Central Asia and beyond to discuss network connectivity and internet infrastructure development.

item.title: Andijan to free up 30 administrative buildings for business development
item.description: Andijan will repurpose 30 administrative buildings for business use, freeing up 13 hectares of land and 70,000 square meters of space. This initiative, involving the relocation of state organizations to the city of Bobur, is expected to attract $1 billion in investments.

item.title: Germany offers 800 nursing positions for Uzbek healthcare workers
item.description: Uzbekistan's mid-level healthcare professionals are invited to work in German clinics through the Globogate program, which offers 800 job openings. Participants will receive 10 months of free German language courses, covering tuition, accommodation, and B2 certification. All visa, travel, and transfer costs are also covered.

item.title: World Bank: Security spending exceeds other sectors in Taliban administration
item.description: A World Bank report indicates that security spending by the Taliban administration has reached 45.2% of total expenditures this fiscal year. This amount surpasses combined spending on education, health, agriculture, infrastructure, and private sector development. The report also notes a slowdown in Afghanistan's economic momentum.

item.title: Taliban Vow Appropriate Response to Pakistani Attacks
item.description: The Taliban stated that an appropriate response will be given to Pakistan's attacks. This statement follows condemnation of Pakistani airstrikes on Afghan provinces by former President Hamid Karzai and the Taliban themselves.

item.title: Tajikistan and FAO discuss food safety and agricultural development
item.description: Tajikistan's Committee for Food Security met with FAO representatives to discuss strengthening cooperation in food safety and agricultural production. Key topics included livestock health, inter-sectoral collaboration, animal disease prevention, and the 'One Health' principles. Discussions also covered plant protection and digitalization in the agricultural sector.

item.title: Zelenskyy tells UN Putin is a 'zero patient' spreading war, urges peace talks
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy addressed the UN, calling Russian President Vladimir Putin a 'zero patient' spreading the idea of war. He emphasized the need for peace, stating that decisions on the battlefield should not determine outcomes. Zelenskyy highlighted Russia's territorial ambitions despite its vast landmass.

item.title: European Council President stresses freedom of navigation through Strait of Hormuz
item.description: European Council President Antonio Costa urged Iran to cooperate with the IAEA and end attacks on neighbors, stressing freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. He emphasized dialogue for peace and stated the EU is ready to support diplomatic efforts to resolve tensions with the US.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 1.1 Billion Som Embezzled in Liquid Soap Purchase in Samarqand
item.description: Officials in the School Education Department of Samarqand region purchased liquid soap at inflated prices, leading to the embezzlement of 1.1 billion som in budget funds. A criminal case has been initiated under Article 167 of the Criminal Code for embezzlement. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: CENTCOM Reports 115 Commercial Vessels Rerouted Due to Iran Naval Blockade
item.description: The U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) reported that 115 commercial vessels were forced to reroute in regional waters as part of a naval blockade of Iran. This action aims to enforce the blockade, which was launched in response to Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
